articles.title: Can You Launch a Beauty Product Without Controversy?
articles.summary: In the endless sea of launches, it feels like drama is the only way to break through the noise. But is it worth it?
articles.body:
Multiple beauty brands faced controversies over product names and packaging similarities, sparking social media debates and discussions.

The beauty industry saw a surge in controversies and disputes, including accusations of copying, lack of credit, and insensitive marketing campaigns.

Brands like Jones Road and Tarte navigated through controversies, with some successfully addressing issues while others faced backlash for their marketing strategies.

It all started with Molly Sims in tears.

In case you aren't as personally invested in beauty's drama du jour, I'll explain: Just over a week ago, the supermodel and founder of YISE Beauty shared a video to Instagram, venting to her one million followers about how an unnamed female-founded brand launched a product with the same name as YISE's Wide Awake Brightening Eye Cream . The likes of Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson offered words of support. Commenters quickly determined that the brand in question was Jones Road, founded by Bobbi Brown, which recently launched Wide Awake Brightening Concealer and Wide Awake Brightening Neutralizer .

But before it could even be resolved, another so-called scandal was brewing: Just after Fenty Skin announced their Dew N Plump Fresh-Sliced Hydrogel Eye Patches in "first of its kind" packaging, influencers posted identical samples from Glow Recipe. And then Huda Beauty. Finally, Vitamasques revealed that they too had the same packaging slated for an upcoming launch. The situation quickly got the meme treatment , with brands from Burger King to BaubleBar joining in with AI-generated eye patches.

Still, there was more: Actor Kim Sensor accused MAC Cosmetics of not giving her proper due for popularizing the "anti-blush" trend , which they've promoted over the last month. And Eadem shared a (rather classy) statement after a white male creator suggested the Black- and Asian-women-founded brand didn't include enough men in their marketing.

Those who follow the industry closely are used to ragebait, controversy, and discourse. But over the last week or so, something shifted: The sheer volume of controversies became so hard to follow, I started to disengage altogether.

Take "Eyepatchgate," as it became known. As each brand announced their nearly identical products, it started to feel like we were being pranked by Big Skincare. Worse: Packaging that felt innovative and exciting mere hours ago was already feeling stale before it was even released.

Huda Beauty, for their part, is already changing course. Founder Huda Kattan wrote in an Instagram comment that the brands were "screwed over by the same packaging supplier" and that "we are not launching it anymore." For what it's worth, Glow Recipe co-founder and co-CEO Christine Chang pushed back on that idea, telling BeautyMatter , "I don't think it's a screwed-over situation; it's more like we saw an innovation we were very excited about it, and it looks like other brands got excited about it as well, right?"

"Those who follow the industry closely are used to ragebait, controversy, and discourse. But over the last week or so, something shifted: The sheer volume of controversies became so hard to follow, I started to disengage altogether."

It's only natural for founders to be protective of their brands. But when they're hot to post, it can sometimes be counterproductive. In the case of Sims and YISE, the tearful (and now deleted) selfie video was successful in the short term—Jones Road agreed to change their product names and it certainly got people talking—but may have backfired in the end. The comments in a post poking fun of the whole kerfuffle are filled with people pointing out that YISE's branding is similar to both Nécessaire's and YSL's. (The brand—pronounced wise —was originally spelled YSE, but was renamed when YSL Beauty opposed the trademark for YSE Beauty.) Nocturnal Skincare co-founder Daniel Kiyoi also shared a video alleging YISE copied their knot bag, without acknowledging the design's Japanese heritage.

Sims's decision to post on Instagram instead of reaching out to Brown directly also had many scratching their heads. "I think that she was probably emotional and posted in the heat of the moment, not really thinking of the backlash that she would receive from it," says Kirbie Johnson, co-host of the Gloss Angeles podcast and writer of Ahead of the Kirb on Substack. "If she does feel like something was infringed upon, I think you owe it to the person to go to them first before taking things public, regardless of what the situation is," she adds, noting that Brown previously appeared on Sims's podcast Lipstick on the Rim .

Ultimately, the naming debacle could have been the best thing to happen for Jones Road. "We wanted to take a moment to share how grateful we are," they shared on Instagram last week. "Not just for our community but also for those who didn't necessarily know of our brand before this week."

It begs the question: If brands are using controversy to break through in an increasingly crowded space, perhaps the old adage that "all press is good press" holds up.

That being said, Jones Road was an involuntary participant in the drama, and cleared things up quickly. It can be risky for brands to get too messy. "I think that brands have too much to lose if public sentiment turns against them, so I really don't think people are going into it trying to create a splash," says Johnson.

Case in point: Back in May, celebrity makeup artist and founder Patrick Ta was accused of profiting off of a smaller Black creator when he launched his Transition Blush, a look popularized by makeup artist Ngozi "Esther" Edeme a.k.a. @paintedbyesther . Although Edeme has a substantial following in her own right, Ta is an industry force; he eventually apologized, and the ordeal seems to be in the past—but Ta still received negative comments on TikTok even months later.

"I think that brands have too much to lose if public sentiment turns against them, so I really don't think people are going into it trying to create a splash."

On the other hand, one brand that has built a Teflon-like reputation for controversy is Tarte—and it seems to be working in their favor. Their brand trips are routinely a social media lightning rod, and in 2024, they were called out for sending some influencers Hermès bracelets, while others received boxes of Cheez-Its and candy. Most recently, Tarte received backlash around the campaign for their Snatch Stick Cream Contour , inspired by cosmetic surgery. The PR boxes featured recipients' photos marked up with lines for different imagined "procedures."

Crisis communications and PR professional Andy Barr described the campaign to Modern Retail as "less like a beauty launch and more like a masterclass in rage-bait marketing," adding that "It is very much the latest in faux-troversial marketing, and the internet is quickly seeing through it."

But Johnson views the Snatch Stick campaign less as ragebait and more as an oversight. "I do understand the vision [they were going for]," she says, adding that "It's really hard to think of every possible thing that could happen, and also makes it like less exciting when all you're thinking about is how someone could misinterpret something or how something could be taken in bad faith."

It's true that brands can't always have eyes on everything everywhere all at once. And from the looks of it the near-constant launches aren't going anywhere. So, perhaps we could all stand to bring the temperature down a notch or two.

Take the eye patch debacle, which became an unexpected "Kumbaya" moment. "I think the way Fenty and the rest of those brands are handling this is the best you can do," says Johnson. "You just have to laugh at some point."

"It's really hard to think of every possible thing that could happen, and also makes it like less exciting when all you're thinking about is how someone could misinterpret something or how something could be taken in bad faith.""

I'll never argue that we should stop dissecting or discussing the topics that truly matter. Credit should go where it's due, and there is always room for the industry to move forward—especially in a time when DEI initiatives are ending by the day. There are genuine issues plaguing the beauty industry, and ones we need to work on fixing.

It begs the question: When everything becomes a discourse, how do we know what's really worth talking about?

articles.title: Acre cria 400 empregos formais em agosto e mantém saldo positivo | G1
articles.standfirst: Estado teve 120 vagas a mais que em julho, quando o saldo foi de 280 empregos. Dados do Caged mostram que foram 4.936 admissões e 4.536 desligamentos.
articles.summary: Estado teve 120 vagas a mais que em julho, quando o saldo foi de 280 empregos. Dados do Caged mostram que foram 4.936 admissões e 4.536 desligamentos.
articles.body:
O Acre fechou agosto com saldo positivo de 400 empregos com carteira assinada , segundo dados do Cadastro Geral de Empregados e Desempregados (Caged), divulgados pelo Ministério do Trabalho e Emprego na última terça-feira (29).

O resultado representa um aumento de 42,9% em relação a julho , quando o estado registrou 280 vagas , e mantém a sequência de saldos positivos pelo sétimo mês consecutivo.

Ao todo, foram 4.936 admissões e 4.536 desligamentos no estado em agosto. Com o resultado, o estoque de empregos formais, que corresponde ao total de vínculos de trabalho com carteira assinada, chegou a 113.179.

O resultado de agosto interrompeu a desaceleração registrada em julho, quando o saldo de empregos caiu 71,4% em relação a junho, que teve 980 vagas . Apesar da recuperação, o número de agosto ainda ficou abaixo do registrado que foi registrado em junho.

O estado começou 2026 com saldo negativo de 829 empregos em janeiro . A partir de fevereiro, porém, passou a registrar mais admissões do que desligamentos, mantendo o resultado positivo nos meses seguintes. ( Veja tabela abaixo )

Entre os setores da economia , os serviços aparecem como destaque nos dados de agosto, com saldo positivo de 211 vagas , conforme o levantamento informado. O resultado indica que o setor teve mais contratações do que demissões no período.

A agropecuária também terminou o período no positivo, com nove vagas , resultado de 12 admissões e 3 desligamentos. O comércio abriu oito postos de trabalho , após registrar 649 contratações e 641 demissões.

Na contramão, a construção teve saldo negativo de 20 vagas , com 83 admissões e 103 desligamentos .

A indústria também fechou o mês no vermelho, com oito postos a menos , resultado de 117 contratações e 125 demissões.

Já na divisão por sexo, homens e mulheres tiveram o mesmo saldo de empregos formais em agosto , com 200 vagas para cada grupo.

Entre os homens, foram registradas 2.869 admissões e 2.669 desligamentos . Já entre as mulheres, houve 2.067 contratações e 1.867 demissões.

Acre cria 400 empregos formais em agosto e mantém saldo positivo pelo 7º mês seguido — Foto: Reprodução

O saldo de empregos também variou entre os municípios acreanos. Bujari registrou o maior resultado positivo , com 235 vagas, após 357 admissões e 122 desligamentos. Em seguida, aparecem Sena Madureira, com 94 postos, e Brasiléia, com 49.

Rio Branco concentrou o maior volume de movimentações no estado, com 3.260 admissões e 3.214 desligamentos. Mesmo com o número elevado de contratações, a capital terminou agosto com saldo positivo de apenas 46 empregos.

No país, o saldo de empregos com carteira assinada também ficou positivo em agosto. Segundo o Caged, foram criadas 165.827 vagas , resultado de 2.294.563 admissões e 2.128.736 desligamentos.

O número foi superior ao registrado em agosto de 2025, quando o país abriu 154.827 vagas formais. De janeiro a agosto deste ano, o saldo nacional chegou a 1.134.033 empregos, uma queda de 25,2% em relação ao mesmo período do ano passado.

Os dados do Caged consideram apenas os vínculos formais de trabalho e, por isso, não representam o total de pessoas ocupadas no país.

O levantamento também não deve ser confundido com a taxa de desemprego calculada pelo Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE), que considera outras formas de ocupação.

articles.title: Médica que teve 50% do corpo queimado em explosão de lancha agradece nova chance: “O que importa é estar viva"  | G1
articles.standfirst: Maize Oliveira passou por cinco cirurgias e ficou internada por dez dias na Unidade de Terapia Intensiva (UTI). Incêndio na lancha aconteceu no domingo (20) e outras 11 pessoas ficaram feridas.
articles.summary: Maize Oliveira passou por cinco cirurgias e ficou internada por dez dias na Unidade de Terapia Intensiva (UTI). Incêndio na lancha aconteceu no domingo (20) e outras 11 pessoas ficaram feridas.
articles.body:
A médica goiana Maize Oliveira, de 34 anos, que teve 50% do corpo queimado após a explosão de uma lancha no Distrito Federal , apresentou evolução no quadro de saúde e foi transferida para um quarto do Hospital de Queimaduras de Goiânia na quinta-feira (1º). Ao g1, a empresária Taize Proto, irmã da dermatologista, contou que a médica está grata pela recuperação e pela oportunidade de continuar o tratamento após deixar a UTI.

“O que importa é estar viva. É ter uma nova chance. É poder continuar.” A frase foi dita por Maize à irmã durante o período de internação e marcou Taize diante da recuperação da médica.

O incêndio na lancha aconteceu no domingo (20), no Lago Paranoá. Segundo informações do Corpo de Bombeiros do Distrito Federal (CBMDF), 11 pessoas ficaram feridas ou sofreram queimaduras leves. Na embarcação, havia outras 14 pessoas. Maize já passou por cinco cirurgias , sendo as duas últimas realizadas na segunda-feira (28) e na quinta-feira (1º).

Em um vídeo gravado no quarto do hospital após deixar a Unidade de Terapia Intensiva (UTI), Maize comemorou a melhora no estado de saúde e falou sobre a felicidade de estar fora da UTI, apesar de ainda precisar passar por novas cirurgias.

“Gente, pensa nessa carinha de felicidade de quem saiu da UTI. Estou no quarto do hospital, graças a Deus, muito melhor clinicamente. As lesões melhoraram bastante também. Ainda tenho algumas cirurgias para realizar, mas estou muito feliz”, disse.

Na gravação, a médica também agradeceu o atendimento prestado pelos profissionais da unidade de saúde onde está internada. Ela lembrou que passou pelo hospital em 2023, durante a graduação, e pediu apoio e orações para as próximas etapas do tratamento.

“Estou muito grata pela equipe que está cuidando de mim. Essa mensagem é para pedir para vocês continuarem orando, porque ainda temos mais cirurgias, mas eu tenho fé que, se Deus quiser, logo, logo tudo isso se acaba”, finalizou.

Em vídeo, a médica Maize afirmou estar melhor clinicamente, embora ainda precise passar por novas cirurgia — Foto: Reprodução/Redes sociais de Maize

Família se prepara para longo período de recuperação

Ao g1 , Taize falou que a médica tem apresentado boa estabilidade emocional e segue sob os cuidados da equipe multiprofissional.

“Emocionalmente, Maize está bem. Tem recebido muito carinho, atenção e está sendo acompanhada por uma equipe médica extremamente preparada, e tudo isso tem feito muita diferença na recuperação dela. Ainda teremos longos dias de hospital pela frente, com muitos cuidados e procedimentos, mas seguimos confiantes e agradecidos por cada evolução”, completou a irmã, agradecendo pelas mensagens e orações recebidas.

De acordo com Taize, também há uma expectativa da família pela recuperação da irmã que, segundo ela, mesmo depois de receber alta hospitalar, enfrentará um longo período de recuperação. Maize mora em Goiânia, mas é natural de Rio Verde, no sudoeste do estado, onde reside sua família.

“Como a Maize mora em Goiânia, vamos precisar mobilizar a família para que ela tenha sempre alguém por perto e todo o suporte necessário. Mesmo em casa, ela ainda precisará ir ao hospital praticamente todos os dias, por muitos meses, para fazer os curativos e acompanhar a evolução das queimaduras”, disse.

articles.title: Urna de lona: a história do inventor que nunca votou na criação | G1
articles.standfirst: Filho de mãe brasileira, Abílio Cesarino cresceu em Jaú (SP) e aproveitou a experiência na fabricação de malas e artigos de couro para desenvolver o modelo que seria usado nas eleições brasileiras por mais de quatro décadas.
articles.summary: O inventor Abílio Cesarino usou sua experiência com malas para criar a urna de lona, modelo que garantiu a segurança das eleições no Brasil por décadas.
articles.body:
Compacta, rápida e acessível. A urna eletrônica já faz parte da rotina de votação dos brasileiros há exatos 30 anos.

Antes da chegada da tecnologia, porém, o destino político do país foi depositado por mais de quatro décadas nas tradicionais urnas de lona , utilizadas de 1955 até o início dos anos 2000, quando o sistema eletrônico chegou a 100% dos municípios brasileiros.

Urna de Lona, invenção de Abílio Cesaríno — Foto: Marcelo Risso/TV TEM

O projeto da urna de lona nasceu da mente do empresário Abílio Cesarino, italiano, filho de mãe brasileira de família jauense, que aproveitou a experiência na fabricação de malas e artefatos de couro para criar um equipamento que ajudaria a moldar a história eleitoral do Brasil.

Contudo, a história carrega uma curiosa ironia. Abílio jamais pôde votar na própria criação. Por ter nascido na Itália e nunca ter se naturalizado brasileiro, ele nunca exerceu o direito ao voto no país.

Na década de 1950, o sistema eleitoral brasileiro enfrentava problemas de logística e de segurança. As votações eram realizadas em urnas pesadas, feitas de madeira e ferro, difíceis de transportar e suscetíveis a violações.

O cenário se tornou ainda mais delicado após o suicídio do presidente Getúlio Vargas, em agosto de 1954, em um período marcado por forte tensão política e incertezas no país.

Em entrevista ao g1 , o historiador Fábio Grossi explica que o combate às fraudes eleitorais ganhou ainda mais importância naquele contexto, e a Justiça Eleitoral passou a buscar um modelo de urna que fosse, ao mesmo tempo, prático e seguro.

"O Brasil já trazia no seu DNA a preocupação com fraudes. A urna de madeira tinha um compartimento inferior de onde se tiravam os votos, e isso era muito manipulado. Na época, a Justiça Eleitoral buscou algo revolucionário e inviolável", afirma o historiador.

Evolução das urnas eleitorais brasileiras — Foto: Reprodução

Foi nesse contexto que entrou em cena Abílio Cesarino. Nascido em 1914, na Itália, ele passou praticamente toda a infância em Jaú (SP). No início dos anos 1950, mudou-se para São Paulo com o irmão, Silvio, e os dois abriram uma fábrica de malas, carteiras e artigos de couro.

Ao saber do concurso lançado pelo governo federal, Abílio percebeu que a técnica utilizada no dia a dia para estruturar malas de viagem poderia ser adaptada para criar uma urna leve, resistente e capaz de guardar com segurança as cédulas de papel.

Abílio Cesaríno, inventor da Urna de Lona — Foto: Reprodução/Marcelo Risso/TV TEM

O projeto, porém, quase não saiu do papel. Empenhado em aperfeiçoar o protótipo, Abílio perdeu o prazo oficial de inscrição no concurso.

Ainda assim, o empresário não desistiu. Ele procurou diretamente o secretário do Tribunal Regional Eleitoral (TRE) para apresentar a criação.

"Ele disse ao tribunal: 'A minha urna é muito melhor que essa que venceu'. Quando o secretário observou a praticidade do protótipo, feito de lona dobrável, percebeu que era perfeita e o projeto foi acatado", conta Grossi.

Aprovado pelo Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE), o projeto da urna de lona teve a patente doada gratuitamente por Abílio ao governo federal. O inventor, no entanto, fez uma única exigência, motivada pelo orgulho que tinha de suas raízes no interior de SP. Ele pediu que o lote inicial de 70 urnas fosse enviado para Jaú.

Com isso, nas eleições presidenciais de 1955, que elegeram Juscelino Kubitschek, Jaú se tornou a primeira cidade do interior do Brasil a utilizar a novidade, estreando o modelo ao lado das grandes capitais.

Urna de lona e ata da votação que elegeu presidente JK — Foto: Nalu Cardoso/g1 RR

Até se aposentar, em 1976, Abílio chegou a produzir em sua fábrica mais de 100 mil urnas de lona, que abasteceram seções eleitorais de todo o país.

Apesar de ter criado um equipamento que fez parte do exercício da cidadania de milhões de brasileiros, Abílio Cesarino nunca pôde depositar oficialmente um voto na própria criação.

Filho de pai italiano e mãe brasileira, Abílio nasceu em Sapri, na Itália, em 1914, durante uma viagem da família, que já morava em Jaú,para visitar parentes na Europa.

Abílio, contudo, permaneceu cidadão italiano e nunca se naturalizou brasileiro, condição necessária para que pudesse exercer o direito de voto no país.

"Tem entrevista dele em que ele brincava que nasceu na Itália 'por acidente', porque a mãe estava grávida e o pai quis fazer a viagem. Ele voltou para Jaú ainda nenê, fez a vida aqui, se considerava jauense, mas nunca votou no Brasil", finalizou o historiador Fábio Grossi.

Abílio Cesarino morreu em 2002, aos 88 anos, e está sepultado no Cemitério Municipal de Jaú.

articles.title: Planilhas de 'BU' a R$ 500: como PF descobriu esquema de Jalser Renier | G1
articles.standfirst: Documentos apreendidos pela Polícia Federal em outra operação detalharam pagamentos de até R$ 4,2 milhões para mais de 12 mil eleitores. Mãe do candidato também foi alvo de buscas.
articles.summary: Documentos apreendidos pela Polícia Federal em outra operação detalharam pagamentos de até R$ 4,2 milhões para mais de 12 mil eleitores. Mãe do candidato também foi alvo de buscas.
articles.body:
Planilhas escondidas em uma mochila no closet do candidato a deputado estadual Jalser Renier (PSDB) revelaram o esquema milionário que previa compra de votos de mais de 12 mil eleitores em Roraima. O material, apreendido pela Polícia Federal (PF), detalhou pagamentos de até R$ 500 a eleitores sob a sigla "BU" , referência direta à "Boca de Urna" .

Em nota, a defesa do candidato informou que "está tomando as medidas legais para restabelecer a liberdade".

Entenda🔎: As planilhas foram achadas pela PF durante buscas de outra operação, no dia 24 de setembro, e motivaram a prisão preventiva dele, nesta quinta-feira (1º), na Operação Lemming . Jalser é apontado como chefe de um esquema que planejava gastar mais de R$ 4,2 milhões com a compra de votos. É a segunda vez que ele é preso em uma semana.

A análise dos documentos revelou um sistema estruturado para pagar eleitores . As planilhas continham campos padronizados como "BU DEFINIDO" , "QTD" e "TOTAL" , e detalhavam valores de R$ 200 , R$ 300 , R$ 400 e R$ 500 por pessoa.

Ao todo, o sistema contabilizava 12.175 eleitores cadastrados e um orçamento de R$ 4.228.100 para bancar a compra de votos e pagar lideranças . Apenas para a reta final de setembro, o grupo reservou a quantia exata de R$ 2.449.300 , registrada exclusivamente sob a sigla "BU" .

A estrutura ilícita visava beneficiar tanto a candidatura de Jalser como a da esposa dele e candidata a deputada federal, Tatyanne Aguillera Padilha, a Dra. Taty (PSDB) . O g1 procurou a defesa dos citados e aguarda retorno.

Os documentos foram achados durante a Operação Filargíria , quando agentes da PF cumpriram um mandado de busca e apreensão na casa de Jalser, no bairro Canarinho, em Boa Vista. A ação era referente a outro processo , expedido pela Justiça estadual comum, que apurava suspeitas de lavagem de dinheiro e desvio de recursos públicos.

No entanto, durante buscas no quarto do candidato os policiais encontraram :

Folhas de anotações e R$ 19,1 mil em dinheiro vivo, junto com documentos pessoais de Jalser Renier;

Planilhas com todo o mapeamento financeiro e territorial da campanha, abaixo da televisão.

Por isso, mesmo que a ação original não tenha sido motivada por compra de votos, os indícios de crimes eleitorais foram validados e repassadas à Justiça Eleitoral, resultando na operação desta quinta (1º).

Durante a prisão em flagrante na outra operação, Jalser assinou um documento onde declarou ser servidor público, com salário mensal de R$ 6.800 e sem outras fontes de renda. A quantia foi considerada incompatível com o orçamento milionário encontrado nos endereços ligados ao candidato.

Ao ser questionado na sede da PF sobre a finalidade das planilhas e do dinheiro, Jalser optou por permanecer em silêncio .

Coordenadores e a mãe de Jalser também foram alvos

Candidato a deputado estadual Jalser Renier (PSDB) e a mãe dele, Itelvina Padilha, foram alvos da PF no dia 1º de outubro — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram

A PF identificou pelo menos 23 pessoas vinculadas às planilhas , mas concentrou as ações em seis coordenadores que gerenciavam as maiores fatias do eleitorado. Todos foram alvos de busca e apreensão e tiveram bens bloqueados na operação desta quinta-feira (1º).

Entre os alvos está Itelvina da Costa Padilha , mãe de Jalser . Ela aparecia nas planilhas como "referência" para intermediar cotas e estava vinculada R$ a 14 mil . Ela mora em um imóvel colado ao escritório político do filho, também no bairro Canarinho.

Os outros coordenadores mapeados e os valores que eles gerenciavam no esquema eram :

Rosilany Maria Marques Pereira Stefanello : Coordenadora de campanha de Jalser. Ela foi alvo de busca e apreensão e teve de R$ 313,8 mil bloqueados.

Marcio Jose Bergmann : Coordenador do esquema no Cantá. Ele foi alvo de busca e apreensão e teve R$ 180 mil bloqueados.

Daniel Cavalcante Rigo : Coordenador do esquema em Caracaraí. Ele foi alvo de busca e apreensão e teve R$ 250 mil bloqueados.

Rosineide Araujo Xavier : Coordenadora do esquema em Boa Vista. Ele foi alvo de busca e apreensão e teve R$ 94 mil bloqueados.

João dos Santos Moura : Coordenador do esquema em Boa Vista. Ele foi alvo de busca e apreensão e teve R$ 66 mil bloqueados.

A defesa da Dra. Taty, Rosilany e Rosineide informou que "aguarda a conclusão das diligencias para adotar as medidas" .

Jalser foi preso no dia 24 de setembro pela PF em Boa Vista, e passou a noite na Penitenciária Agrícola de Monte Cristo (Pamc), por conta dos indícios de compra de votos encontrados no escritório dele.

Renier foi levado à sede da PF, onde prestou depoimento. Em entrevista ao g1 na ocasião, o advogado dele, Carlos Vilareal, disse que entre os documentos apreendidos, havia planilhas com nomes de cabos eleitorais, "apoiadores remunerados" e "voluntários".

Candidato a deputado estadual Jalser Renier em Roraima nas eleições 2026 — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram

Jalser Renier Padilha é um dos políticos mais conhecidos de Roraima. Ele foi deputado por 27 anos , mas teve o mandato cassado pela Assembleia Legislativa de Roraima (ALE-RR) em 2022, por quebra de decoro. A cassação ocorreu após ele ser acusado de ser o mandante do sequestro e da tortura do jornalista Romano dos Anjos, em 2020.

No processo penal sobre o caso do jornalista, ele é réu por sete crimes: sequestro qualificado , tortura qualificada , constituição de milícia privada , dano qualificado , roubo majorado , cárcere privado e violação de domicílio qualificada .

A c assação também havia deixado Jalser inelegível até 2030 . No entanto, em agosto, o ministro Nunes Marques, do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), concedeu uma liminar que suspendeu parcialmente os efeitos da cassação . Com isso, ele ficou autorizado a disputar as eleições deste ano .

articles.title: MPT investiga prefeito de Cotia após denúncia de pressão sobre servidores para fazer campanha de candidato a deputado federal | G1
articles.standfirst: Mensagens e áudio atribuídos a Welington Formiga (PDT) indicam que funcionários que não apoiarem Eduardo Mascarenhas poderão ser exonerados a partir de 5 de outubro; denúncia também foi apresentada ao Ministério Público Eleitoral. Prefeito nega.
articles.summary: Mensagens e áudio atribuídos a Welington Formiga (PDT) indicam que funcionários que não apoiarem Eduardo Mascarenhas poderão ser exonerados a partir de 5 de outubro; denúncia também foi apresentada ao Ministério Público Eleitoral. Prefeito nega.
articles.body:
Welington Formiga (prefeito de Cotia, à esquerda) e Eduardo Mascarenhas (Xaropinho, à direita) posam juntos durante campanha — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram

O prefeito de Cotia, Welington Formiga ( PDT ), é acusado de pressionar secretários e outros integrantes do primeiro escalão da Prefeitura a fazer campanha para Eduardo Mascarenhas (PDT), conhecido por interpretar o personagem de TV Xaropinho e candidato a deputado federal nas eleições de 2026.

Segundo denúncia obtida pelo g1 , Formiga teria afirmado em um grupo de WhatsApp que quem não participasse da campanha de Xaropinho ou apoiasse outros candidatos poderia ser demitido entre os dias 5 e 10 de outubro.

"Ele está ameaçando demitir 100 pessoas, quer que a gente trabalhe para o candidato dele e que não faça campanha para outros candidatos. Isso é coação, é crime! E ele continua, parece que ele não tem limite", declarou uma fonte, que terá a identidade preservada por medo de retaliação.

🔎A legislação eleitoral brasileira garante que o voto é livre e secreto e veda qualquer forma de constrangimento, coação ou pressão para influenciar a escolha dos eleitores. O uso da relação hierárquica no ambiente de trabalho para pedir votos ou cobrar apoio político de subordinados pode caracterizar assédio eleitoral e, dependendo das circunstâncias, abuso de poder político e uso indevido da estrutura pública.

O Ministério Público do Trabalho (MPT ) confirmou que recebeu a denúncia na terça-feira (29), instaurou uma investigação e deverá notificar a Prefeitura de Cotia nas próximas horas. O prefeito Welington Formiga negou as acusações.

A denúncia é acompanhada de mensagens atribuídas ao prefeito em um grupo de WhatsApp usado pelo primeiro escalão do governo. Segundo fontes, o grupo reúne cerca de 105 pessoas, entre secretários titulares e adjuntos, chefes de gabinete e assessores.

Em um dos áudios enviados aos funcionários, o prefeito arquiteta uma possibilidade de eleger dois candidatos tentando convencer os integrantes do grupo (ouça abaixo) .

"Pessoal, vamos lá, para que todo mundo possa entender. Nós estamos, cada um, fazendo um grupo com 30, 50 pessoas. Com o tamanho do nosso grupo, nós vamos ter 30 mil pessoas nos grupos. 30 mil vezes 3 dá? 90! 90 mil votos. Elegemos dois dos nossos deputados. É só a gente querer, 'é só você querer, que amanhã assim será'. Fran Silva, estadual, e Eduardo Xaropinho, federal. Se nós quisermos e nos unirmos, vamos eleger nossos deputados".

Em uma das mensagens de texto enviada às 22h39, Formiga indica que funcionários que não apoiarem Eduardo Mascarenhas poderão deixar a prefeitura a partir de 5 de outubro

"Tem um pessoal que vai começar a me ajudar dia 5 na campanha, aí já poderão apoiar a oposição", escreveu o prefeito, segundo a imagem apresentada à reportagem (veja abaixo) .

Mensagens atribuídas a Welington Formiga em conversas de grupo de WhatsApp da prefeitura de Cotia — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

Outros prints da abordagem do prefeito aos secretários:

Denúncia aponta pressão sobre mais de 100 servidores

Pessoas que fizeram a denúncia afirmaram que a pressão ocorre desde 2025, mas teria aumentado durante o período eleitoral.

Segundo elas, Formiga utilizaria o grupo de WhatsApp para cobrar publicações, compartilhamentos e vídeos de apoio ao candidato nas redes sociais.

Integrantes da equipe também teriam sido orientados a se cadastrar para atuar na campanha e que mensagens de outros funcionários no grupo indicavam que os cadastros haviam sido feitos.

Ainda segundo a denúncia, Formiga teria cobrado que secretários e assessores se tornassem "coordenadores" da campanha e encaminhado um link para cadastro.

Secretários foram demitidos e recontratados

Dois secretários foram exonerados em 6 de setembro e retornaram aos cargos três dias depois, em 9 de setembro, após manifestações de apoio a outros candidatos (veja abaixo) .

Mensagens atribuídas a Welington Formiga — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

De acordo com o relato, o episódio teria provocado apreensão entre outros integrantes da Prefeitura, que passaram a temer que também fossem demitidos por não fazerem propaganda para Eduardo Mascarenhas. A fonte afirma que o funcionário demitido relatou ter recebido ligações de outros secretários preocupados com a possibilidade de perder o cargo.

"Ontem [dia 30] à noite, me ligaram dizendo que mais três pessoas estão desesperadas achando que vão ser demitidas por não fazerem propaganda do candidato. Logo depois à ligação, essas mesmas pessoas postaram vídeos do Xaropinho", disse a fonte.

Reuniões para campanha durante o expediente

Outra acusação apresentada ao Ministério Público é a de que servidores teriam sido convocados para reuniões de campanha em horário de expediente.

Segundo o denunciante, funcionários da Prefeitura foram divididos em grupos para participar de encontros às 17h30, 19h e 21h em um posto na Granja Viana, bairro nobre de Cotia.

Nessas reuniões, os servidores foram orientados a gravar vídeos de apoio ao candidato.

Na avaliação apresentada pelo denunciante ao MP, o uso de servidores e da estrutura pública para atividades eleitorais poderia caracterizar abuso de poder político e outras irregularidades. Essas alegações ainda são objeto de apuração.

Procurado pelo g1 , o prefeito negou, por meio de nota, que esteja pressionando secretários ou servidores comissionados a votar ou fazer campanha para candidatos apoiados por ele.

Formiga afirmou que todos os secretários e servidores têm liberdade para apoiar e votar nos candidatos de sua preferência e que jamais condicionaria a permanência ou o trabalho de um servidor à sua posição política.

"[...] Não procede a informação de que estaria pressionando secretários ou servidores comissionados a votar em candidatos por ele apoiados.

Todos os secretários e servidores têm total liberdade para apoiar e votar nos candidatos de sua preferência. O prefeito respeita a escolha de cada pessoa e jamais condicionaria a permanência ou o trabalho de um servidor à sua posição política.

O apoio político do prefeito a determinados candidatos é uma manifestação pessoal e democrática e não deve ser confundida com qualquer forma de pressão ou orientação aos servidores municipais."

Em comunicado, o prefeito diz ainda que seu apoio político a candidatos é uma manifestação pessoal e não deve ser confundido com pressão sobre funcionários da Prefeitura.

Denúncia também foi levada ao Ministério Público Eleitoral

Além do MPT, o servidor afirma ter apresentado uma denúncia ao Ministério Público Eleitoral em 13 de setembro.

Ao g1 , o MPE informou que o procedimento foi encaminhado para análise na Justiça Eleitoral de Cotia, pois os elementos apresentados inicialmente não permitiam identificar se havia, de fato, envolvimento do prefeito nos fatos narrados.

Por isso, em 26 de setembro, houve declínio de atribuições da Procuradoria Regional Eleitoral para a promotoria eleitoral responsável pelo local dos fatos, em Cotia.

A Procuradoria informou ainda que, caso surjam indícios de envolvimento do prefeito, o caso poderá retornar à Procuradoria Regional Eleitoral em razão da prerrogativa de foro.

articles.title: Juiz nega pedido de absolvição de mãe acusada de matar os 3 filhos  | G1
articles.standfirst: Lindsay Clancy, de 36 anos, é acusada de estrangular os filhos, de 5 anos, 3 anos e 8 meses, em 2023; primeiro julgamento terminou sem veredito.
articles.summary: Lindsay Clancy, de 36 anos, é acusada de estrangular os filhos, de 5 anos, 3 anos e 8 meses, em 2023; primeiro julgamento terminou sem veredito.
articles.body:
Lindsay Clancy durante seu julgamento por homicídio. — Foto: AP/Josh Reynolds, Pool

Um juiz negou nesta quinta-feira (1) o pedido de absolvição de Lindsay Clancy, de 36 anos, acusada de matar os três filhos em 2023. A decisão ocorre após o primeiro julgamento da mulher ser anulado porque o júri não conseguiu chegar a um veredito unânime. Com isso, Lindsay deverá enfrentar um novo julgamento.

Clancy é acusada de estrangular os filhos Cora, de 5 anos, Dawson, de 3, e Callan, de 8 meses, na casa da família, em Massachusetts, nos Estados Unidos.

O juiz William Sullivan, do Tribunal de Plymouth, considerou que havia provas suficientes para que um júri pudesse condenar Lindsay. A decisão contraria o argumento apresentado pelo advogado de defesa, Kevin Reddington, que questiona a força das evidências reunidas pela promotoria.

Em uma audiência realizada em 29 de setembro, Reddington também colocou em dúvida a credibilidade das declarações dadas por Lindsay à polícia e questionou a investigação. "Onde estão as provas?", disse o advogado.

Durante o julgamento, Lindsay não negou ter matado os filhos, mas afirmou que sofria de psicose pós-parto e que ouviu uma voz ordenando que matasse as crianças.

Segundo a defesa, a condição de saúde mental teria provocado o comportamento de Lindsay. A psicose pós-parto é uma condição rara que, segundo especialistas médicos, afeta entre uma e duas mulheres a cada mil partos.

Os promotores, por outro lado, afirmam que Lindsay planejou os assassinatos e que tinha capacidade de compreender as consequências de seus atos. A promotora Jennifer Sprague classificou como "ridículo" o argumento de Reddington de que não havia provas suficientes contra a acusada.

A contestação, pela defesa, das próprias declarações de Lindsay representa uma mudança em relação à estratégia apresentada durante o julgamento, que se concentrou principalmente na alegação de psicose pós-parto.

O julgamento foi anulado em 4 de setembro, depois que os jurados não conseguiram chegar a um veredito unânime. O caso provocou um debate nos Estados Unidos sobre saúde mental materna e psicose pós-parto.

Lindsay está internada em uma instituição psiquiátrica. Ela se declarou inocente das acusações.

Após as mortes, Lindsay cortou o próprio pescoço e os pulsos e pulou da janela do segundo andar da residência. Ela sobreviveu à tentativa de suicídio, mas ficou paralisada da cintura para baixo.

Lindsay Clancy 'disse que ouviu uma voz masculina ordenando que ela matasse seus filhos', segundo o testemunho de um psicólogo aos jurados. — Foto: Getty Images via BBC

articles.title: Ethiopia and Eritrea cut diplomatic ties as Tigray conflict escalates
articles.summary: The diplomatic fallout comes as Ethiopian forces battle rebel fighters across its northern region.
articles.body:
Ethiopia and Eritrea have severed diplomatic relations as renewed fighting in northern Ethiopia raises fears of a wider regional conflict.

On Thursday, Ethiopia announced that it was closing its embassy in the Eritrean capital, Asmara, and ordered 10 Eritrean diplomats to leave the country within 48 hours, accusing them of activities that threatened national security.

Eritrea responded by cutting diplomatic relations, saying Ethiopia's decision had left it with no choice but to take reciprocal action.

The diplomatic confrontation came hours after powerful explosions were heard overnight in Ethiopian capital, Addis Ababa , including near Ethiopia's military headquarters.

It follows a sharp deterioration in relations between the neighbours, with Ethiopia accusing Eritrea of supporting a new rebel alliance – an allegation Asmara has repeatedly denied.

Eritrea described the decision to expel its ambassador as "astounding".

"Eritrea has no option but to reciprocate in kind and sever all diplomatic ties with Ethiopia," its foreign ministry said, warning of "negative corollaries" from the decision.

The diplomatic fallout comes as Ethiopian federal forces battle fighters from the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) and its allies across parts of the northern regions of Tigray, Afar and Amhara.

Ethiopia has also expelled an Egyptian diplomat, giving him 48 hours to leave the country, according to state media. The government has not publicly given a reason for the decision.

Egypt responded by ordering an Ethiopian embassy official to leave within the same period, according to the state-affiliated Al Qahera News.

Relations between Ethiopia and Egypt have been strained for years, largely over Ethiopia's Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam (GERD), a huge hydroelectric project on the Blue Nile.

Egypt, which relies heavily on the Nile for its water supplies, has long expressed concern about the dam's potential impact on its share of the river's water.

How fresh fighting in Tigray could spark wider conflict in Ethiopia

WATCH: Why are Ethiopia's rebels joining forces?

The cutting of ties between Ethiopia and Eritrea mark a dramatic reversal from 2018, when Abiy restored relations with Asmara after two decades of hostility, prompting joyous scenes as the border reopened and families separated for years were reunited.

The rapprochement helped earn the Ethiopian prime minister the Nobel Peace Prize in 2019.

The latest hostilities are the most serious since a peace agreement ended the devastating Tigray war in 2022. An African Union mediator previously estimated that about 600,000 people had died during that two-year conflict.

Last month, the TPLF joined six other armed movements, including the Fano militia from Amhara, to form an alliance whose stated objective is to remove Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's government from power.

A pro-government militia commander fighting in Tigray told the BBC that Eritrean soldiers had been involved on the front lines.

The BBC has not independently verified the allegation.

The BBC is unable to report from Tigray and the internet has been cut, making it difficult to get reliable information from the region. It is not clear who was responsible for cutting communications.

In a rare response to the BBC before diplomatic relations were severed, Eritrea's Information Minister Yemane Gebremeskel denied that it was involved in the fighting in Tigray, which borders his country.

He told BBC Tigrinya that Ethiopia's governing Prosperity Party was blaming neighbouring countries to divert attention from conflicts and other problems within Ethiopia.

The two countries were allies during the 2020-2022 Tigray war, when Eritrean troops fought alongside Ethiopian federal forces against the TPLF.

But relations have deteriorated significantly since then, particularly over Ethiopia's push for direct access to the Red Sea.

Ethiopia lost its coastline when Eritrea became independent in 1993.

Abiy has repeatedly argued that access to the sea is essential to Ethiopia's long-term economic and security interests, while Eritrea has accused his government of harbouring ambitions over its ports.

Federal forces and their allies appear to have made gains in southern Tigray and are advancing towards Mekelle, the regional capital. In Alamata, a doctor told the BBC earlier this week that at least 52 civilians had been killed during three days of intense fighting.

The TPLF has also been fighting in neighbouring Afar, which lies along Ethiopia's crucial transport corridor to Djibouti and the sea. Tens of thousands of people are estimated to have fled their homes there.

Both the Ethiopian government and the TPLF accuse the other of starting the latest hostilities. Tigrayan authorities say their forces were responding to a federal offensive and drone strikes, while Addis Ababa says Tigrayan fighters launched attacks after taking control of federally administered airports in Tigray.

The African Union has urged Ethiopia, Eritrea and Egypt to exercise restraint and resolve their differences through diplomatic channels, warning against actions that could further destabilise the region.

The UN has also warned that the deteriorating security situation is severely disrupting humanitarian work in northern Ethiopia. UN spokesman Stéphane Dujarric said drone activity and air strikes were putting civilians, vital infrastructure and aid operations at risk, while insecurity and road closures were restricting humanitarian movements.

The UN has called on all sides to guarantee safe and unhindered access to people in need.

articles.title: Greece pushes EU to suspend asylum during mass migration surges
articles.summary: EU migration pact improvements face criticism for insufficient tools to manage large-scale migration emergencies.
articles.body:
Greece has urged the European Union to allow member states to temporarily suspend asylum applications during periods of mass migration, arguing that current rules cannot handle emergencies such as the surge in Spain’s North African enclave of Ceuta this summer.

The proposal was submitted to EU interior ministers meeting in Luxembourg on Thursday during the Justice and Home Affairs Council, and appeared to draw support from some member states.

Greek Migration Minister Thanos Plevris said the EU’s migration pact, which took effect in June, had improved the bloc’s ability to manage migration flows but had not gone far enough.

“In such cases, there should be enhanced border surveillance and suspension of asylum,” he told reporters ahead of the meeting.

Dutch Migration Minister Bart van den Brink backed the approach, saying mass arrivals like those in Ceuta should be “treated as a border management issue rather than an asylum issue”.

Spain estimates more than 72,000 migrants entered Ceuta in late July. While most have since returned, about 10,000 remain, reinforcing calls in some European capitals for a tougher approach.

Anti-immigration sentiment has remained a potent political force across Europe since more than a million people, many of them Syrians fleeing war, arrived in the bloc in 2015. The influx boosted support for nationalist and far-right parties and pushed many governments towards more restrictive migration policies centred on border controls, deterrence and returns.

Irregular arrivals are down 35 percent this year, while returns rose about 8 percent in the first half of the year.

Several member states argue that although the migration pact has helped reduce arrivals, it still lacks sufficient tools to handle large-scale emergencies, despite containing mechanisms intended for such situations.

Plevris’s proposal comes two weeks after European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said the commission would present an emergency framework allowing member states to respond to sudden, large-scale arrivals.

EU Migration Commissioner Magnus Brunner said international law would still have to be respected. “Europe needs the means to protect its borders at all times,” he said. “When movements are engineered and weaponised against us, this is not just a migration issue; it is a security issue … Of course we will always comply with fundamental rights and values.”

Ministers also approved a new return regulation on Thursday allowing member states to establish return hubs outside the EU.

Two European Parliament politicians said Rwanda has held preliminary talks with some EU countries about hosting such a facility, citing discussions with Rwandan officials.

Officials from Greece, the Netherlands, Germany, Austria and Denmark, known as the Group of Five, met on the sidelines of the council on Thursday. Van den Brink said a technical mission visited the potential host country in early September, and the group aims to identify it by the end of this year, with transfers beginning in 2027.

articles.title: Miami judge rules federal noncitizen voting law violates US Constitution
articles.summary: Judge Leibowitz’s decision underscores state jurisdiction over voter qualifications.
articles.body:
A United States federal judge has ruled that a law criminalising voting by noncitizens is unconstitutional, dealing a setback for President Donald Trump’s administration as it cracks down on alleged election fraud ahead of November’s midterm elections .

US District Judge David Leibowitz in Miami dismissed a federal case on Thursday against Chelsea Cox, a Florida resident originally from Jamaica who had been charged in October 2025 with illegally voting in the 2020 presidential election.

Leibowitz, who was nominated to the bench by former Democratic President Joe Biden, found that under the US Constitution, only individual states, not the US Congress, have the authority to set voter qualifications.

Since every state already requires US citizenship to vote, he wrote, it is up to Florida, not the Department of Justice, to prosecute Cox for breaking that rule. “Florida can and does,” he wrote, noting the state already has its own laws against the conduct Cox is accused of.

The ruling applies only to Cox’s case and it does not bind judges elsewhere, though about 45 similar cases remain pending nationwide. At least four other defendants have raised the same constitutional challenge.

Court filings show Cox entered the US as a tourist in 1999, overstayed her visa, and later used a fraudulent birth certificate from the US Virgin Islands, a US territory in the Caribbean, to obtain a Florida driver’s licence and register to vote in 2012.

Trump has falsely claimed that noncitizen voting, which is already illegal and rare, cost him the 2020 election , and has cast it as part of a broader effort by Democrats to dilute Republican support.

The Department of Justice has charged at least 60 people with the offence since Trump returned to office in January 2025.

Among 129 people charged with “voting by an alien” since 2021, none was accused of conspiring to sway an election, backing a candidate, or being paid to vote, according to Reuters. Most were found to be lawful permanent residents who had registered by mistake or on the incorrect advice of an election worker or government clerk.

Cox’s lawyer, Bruce Udolf, welcomed the ruling and said he hoped authorities would not now seek to deport her, citing her declining health conditions.

articles.title: ‘Sat for 11 seconds’: Mystery shrouds Premanand Maharaj disciple’s death after CCTV footage emerges
articles.summary: AGRA: A fresh CCTV video showing the moments before the death of 25-year-old Deepak Lodhi alias Rasik Dulari Sharan, a disciple of Premanand Maharaj, has
articles.body: AGRA: A fresh CCTV video showing the moments before the death of 25-year-old Deepak Lodhi alias Rasik Dulari Sharan, a disciple of Premanand Maharaj, has surfaced, raising questions about the circumstances in which he fell from the fourth floor of a building in Vrindavan's Varah Ghat area.The 33-second video shows Rasik Dulari Sharan sitting on the rooftop for around 11 seconds before suddenly getting up and jumping. Another disciple is seen climbing the stairs towards the rooftop, apparently to approach him, but he jumps before the person can reach him.The incident took place at Gau Kripa Kunj, where disciples of Premanand Maharaj reside. Police are investigating the circumstances surrounding his death and questioning other disciples staying at the building. CCTV footage is also being examined.The video has raised several questions about what happened before Rasik Dulari Sharan reached the rooftop, including reports circulating on social media about an alleged genital injury. Police have not yet established the circumstances leading to his death.Meanwhile, the incident has prompted significant changes in the arrangements at Shri Hit Radha Keli Kunj Ashram in Vrindavan. The ashram has indefinitely suspended final initiation ceremonies and the scheduled attendance of disciples seeking Premanand Maharaj's blessings. The restrictions came into effect on October 1.The dress code for initiated disciples residing in Vrindavan has also been changed. They have been instructed to stop wearing yellow and white clothes and instead dress like ordinary devotees. Only ascetics and the saint's personal attendants will continue wearing the traditional colours.The changes follow the controversy surrounding Athe disciple's death and negative comments on social media. However, an attendant at the ashram's enquiry counter confirmed some of the changes.The impact of the restrictions was visible on Wednesday, when disciples were seen visiting the ashram in ordinary coloured clothes instead of their usual yellow and white attire. articles.title: How the fighting in Ethiopia spread beyond Tigray, in maps and charts
articles.summary: Old rivalries, territorial disputes and new alliances are reshaping the conflict in Ethiopia’s north.
articles.body:
Fighting is intensifying across northern Ethiopia, almost four years after a peace deal ended a devastating two-year war in the country’s Tigray region.

The conflict has also spread into the neighbouring Amhara and Afar regions. Government-aligned forces say they captured the strategic town of Alamata, Tigray, on September 28, while Tigrayan forces have pushed into Afar.

Telecommunications have been cut across much of Tigray and commercial flights have been suspended, separating families and hampering humanitarian operations.

Ethiopia’s army chief has accused Eritrea, Sudan’s army and Egypt of backing the armed groups, raising fears of a wider regional war. All countries have denied the allegations, with Egypt adding that it strictly respects the sovereignty of neighbouring states.

In this visual explainer, Al Jazeera maps where the fighting is, who is involved and how Ethiopia got here.

Fighting is concentrated in three regions in northern Ethiopia: Tigray, Amhara and Afar. There are several active fronts rather than a single battlefield.

In southern Tigray, government forces and their allies have taken Alamata, a strategic town about 120km (75 miles) south of the regional capital, Mekelle.

The town is a supply hub for troops, fuel and food near Tigray’s border with Amhara.

On September 22, between 15 and 17 drone strikes hit Alamata, including several schools and a hospital, according to the conflict monitor ACLED.

To the west, a separate front has opened near the Tekeze River in western Tigray, an area disputed between Tigray and Amhara.

Fighting has also spread into northern Amhara, around Kobo and Gidan in North Wello zone and Sekota in Wag Hemra zone, which government forces retook on September 27.

Further east, Tigrayan forces and the Afar armed group Ugugumo have advanced into Afar, where fighting has been reported along the Tigray-Afar border and around Erebti and Abala.

The advance matters because it could threaten the Semera-Djibouti corridor, Ethiopia’s main route for imports, including fuel.

Seven Ethiopian armed and political groups announced an alliance on September 20 aimed at removing Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed’s government and establishing an inclusive transitional government.

The group is called the Ethiopian Peoples’ Forces Alliance for Survival, or the Alliance for Survival. Its members include:

The Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF) : The alliance’s main military force, whose fighters launched the latest offensive. It dominated Ethiopian politics for nearly three decades before Abiy took office in 2018. War broke out between the TPLF and federal forces in November 2020.

The Amhara Fano National Movement: A coalition of Fano factions that turned against Abiy’s government in 2023, after fighting alongside federal forces during the Tigray war.

The Oromo Liberation Army (OLA): It has fought federal forces in Oromia since 2018, seeking greater self-determination for the Oromo.

The other groups named in the alliance are the Ogaden National Liberation Front (ONLF), the Afar Revolutionary Democratic Unity Front (also known as Ugugumo), the Benishangul Peoples’ Liberation Movement and the Gumuz Peoples’ Democratic Movement. On September 25, the Sidama National Liberation Front announced that it would also join.

The alliance’s membership is contested. According to Jalale Getachew Birru, senior East Africa analyst at ACLED , the Gumuz Peoples’ Democratic Movement has denied joining, saying it has no armed wing. The ONLF is split: one faction backs the alliance, while another says it is not part of it. The OLA has indicated that its main interest is removing the government rather than joining coordinated military operations.

ACLED says only three members, the TPLF, the Amhara Fano National Movement and Ugugumo, were actively fighting federal forces as of September 26.

In its founding statement, the alliance accused the government of “dictatorial rule”. It said a transitional government would end the country’s wars, protect rights and open a national dialogue.

Ethiopia is a landlocked country in the Horn of Africa, bordered by Eritrea, Sudan, South Sudan, Kenya, Somalia and Djibouti. With about 139 million people, it is Africa’s second-most populous country after Nigeria.

It is also one of the world’s most ethnically diverse countries, with more than 80 groups. The Oromo are the largest, making up about 35 percent of the population, followed by the Amhara at about 24 percent. Other major groups include Somali (7 percent), Tigrayan (6 percent) and Sidama (4 percent).

Ethiopia is divided into 12 regional states and two chartered cities, Addis Ababa and Dire Dawa. The federal system, introduced in 1992 and formalised in the 1994 constitution, largely follows ethnic and linguistic divisions.

The renewed fighting stems from political and territorial tensions left unresolved following Ethiopia’s 2020-2022 Tigray war. The Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF) and the federal government remain divided over political control, security and disputed territory.

Tensions have been building for months. According to the conflict monitor ACLED, clashes between Tigrayan and federal forces began near the Sudanese border on August 1, followed by federal drone strikes and Tigrayan troop deployments.

In September, Tigrayan forces moved tanks and artillery south. There were also reports of renewed recruitment and forced mobilisation in Tigray.

On September 20, the TPLF and six other armed and political groups announced the Ethiopian Peoples’ Forces Alliance for Survival, which aims to overthrow Abiy’s government and install a transitional administration.

Three days later, on September 23, fighting escalated sharply. Tigrayan forces seized the airports in Mekelle, Axum and Shire and pushed into neighbouring Afar and Amhara. The government says the TPLF launched an “all-out offensive”. The TPLF says it is fighting a “defensive war” and accuses federal forces of attacking with aircraft, drones and artillery.

articles.title: Former Dallas officer who shot Black man in apartment that she mistook for hers gets parole
articles.summary: A white Dallas police officer convicted of killing a Black man in his apartment that she mistook for her own was granted parole Thursday after serving seven years of her 10-year sentence.
articles.body: A white Dallas police officer convicted of killing a Black man in his apartment that she mistook for her own was granted parole Thursday after serving seven years of her 10-year sentence. The Texas Board of Pardons and Parole, which is appointed by Gov. Greg Abbott, rejected Amber Guyger’s initial parole request in 2024, but approved her case over the objections of victim Botham Jean’s family the first time she was eligible to ask again. Guyger, 38, was convicted of murder in the 2018 killing of 26-year-old Jean, an accountant from the Caribbean island nation of St. Lucia, who had been eating a bowl of ice cream when Guyger entered his home and shot him. Guyger was arrested three days after the shooting and was fired before her murder trial. She had faced up to life in prison or as little as two years. Prosecutors initially asked the jury for a sentence of 28 years. The shooting drew widespread attention because of the strange circumstances and because it was one in a string of shootings of Black men by white police officers. Guyger’s sentencing hearing also included a stunning courtroom scene when Jean’s brother and the Black judge presiding over the case embraced the sobbing Guyger. At trial, Guyger said that after a long shift at work and still in uniform, she walked up to Jean’s apartment — which was on the fourth floor, directly above hers on the third — and found the door unlocked. She said she thought the apartment was her own and that Jean was an intruder when she drew her service weapon and entered. Civil rights attorney Lee Merritt said Thursday that Jean’s family “strongly opposed this parole.” “They stood up again and again to ask that the full sentence be served. A 10-year sentence was already a fraction of what was lost. Releasing Ms. Guyger after seven years makes that loss feel even smaller in the eyes of the system. It is not smaller,” Merritt said. In 2024, a jury ordered Guyger to pay Jean’s family nearly $100 million in a federal civil trial. In granting her release, the board said it reviewed a “plethora” of information in her case. The board said Guyger’s record did not include a documented pattern of violent or assaultive arrests or convictions, and showed she completed programs in her prison treatment plan to get and keep a job when she is released. The board said the state prison system will determine when she is released. Texas Department of Criminal Justice officials did not immediately respond to requests for comment Thursday. Guyger’s legal defense team did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Dallas police said the department played no role in Guyger’s request for parole or the decision to release her. “The Dallas Police Department understands this decision may bring renewed attention and emotion surrounding the tragic death of Botham Jean. Our thoughts remain with the Jean family and all those impacted by his loss,” the department said.

articles.title: Judge denies defense motion asking Lindsay Clancy be found not guilty due to a lack of evidence
articles.summary: The judge in the Lindsay Clancy murder case refused to declare her not guilty, turning down a defense motion that had argued there wasn’t enough evidence to prove she was responsible for killing her three children.
articles.body: BOSTON — The judge in the Lindsay Clancy murder case on Thursday refused to declare her not guilty, turning down a defense motion that had argued there wasn’t enough evidence to prove she was responsible for killing her three children. During Clancy’s first trial, which ended Sept. 4 with a deadlocked jury, her defense argued that she was not criminally responsible because of a mental disease, specifically a rare condition called postpartum psychosis. As such, the defense didn’t dispute that the 36-year-old former labor and delivery nurse carried out the killings at her family’s Massachusetts home in 2023. However, in a hearing earlier this week, Clancy’s attorney Kevin Reddington tried to persuade the judge that prosecutors had not offered any proof that Clancy did it. Prosecutors argued there was plenty of evidence, calling Reddington’s claim “laughable.” Prosecutors have yet to decide whether they will put the case in front of a jury for a second time. They could choose to retry her on first-degree murder charges or seek to try her only on lesser charges, including second-degree murder or manslaughter, or drop the case entirely. In his ruling Thursday, Judge William Sullivan noted that for the purposes of his decision, he was required to analyze the evidence in the light most favorable to prosecutors — and that it was up to the jury, not the judge, to decide whether to believe expert witnesses for the defense who testified that Clancy was not responsible for her actions because of mental illness. “There was evidence introduced, both physical and circumstantial, that would permit a rational trier of fact to find beyond a reasonable doubt the elements of the charge of murder,” Sullivan wrote. At the first trial, prosecutors acknowledged that Clancy had mental health problems that included months of treatment and a stay in a psychiatric hospital, but argued that she knew what she was doing when she strangled the children — the youngest just 8 months old — then tried to kill herself. Sullivan had declared a mistrial with the jury split 11 to 1 in favor of acquitting Clancy of murder charges. In Tuesday’s hearing, Reddington suggested the entire case “was based on speculation” and listed shortcomings in the prosecution’s case. There was almost no police investigation, he claimed, and significant questions revolving around Clancy’s condition outside the night of the killings and her lack of memory of what happened. At the trial, jurors heard testimony that Clancy said she heard voices instructing her to kill 5-year-old Cora, 3-year-old Dawson and 8-month-old Callan Clancy. Her DNA was found on exercise bands used to strangle them. Before the trial, Reddington himself filed a motion in which he said Clancy was willing to stipulate, in writing, to her involvement in the children’s deaths. “For the first time, the defendant is arguing that there is no evidence she did this,” Prosecutor Shanan Buckingham told the judge. “I’d suggest to you the entire record is voluminous as to information supporting the fact that she did this.” Clancy remains charged with murder and is expected to stay at a psychiatric hospital until her case is resolved. Clancy could have been sentenced to life in prison if convicted of murder. If acquitted, the judge could have ordered her confined to a mental health facility. Her former husband, Patrick Clancy, who discovered the children’s bodies, has said in interviews that he forgives her. The livestreamed trial generated intense public interest and drew attention to maternal mental health after childbirth. articles.title: ‘I couldn’t let everybody else die,’ says hero Flydubai pilot Smit Machchhar
articles.summary: Smit Machchhar, the hero Flydubai captain who fought off a savage attack by his copilot, kept fighting because he could not “let everybody else die,” he said in his first public remarks since Wednesday’s suspected hijacking attempt.
articles.body: Smit Machchhar, the hero Flydubai captain who fought off a savage attack by his copilot, kept fighting because he could not “let everybody else die,” he said in his first public remarks since Wednesday’s suspected hijacking attempt. “In that moment, I was fighting for my life,” Machchhar told India’s Prime Minister Narendra Modi in a video call on Friday. “I was so severely wounded that I had fallen down… at that time, I was thinking what if I don’t get up?” A horrific mid-air catastrophe on flight FZ 1073 heading to Tel Aviv was averted in a stunning turn of events on Wednesday when passengers bravely rushed into the cockpit and stand-in pilots regained control of the aircraft. Machchhar was badly injured while trying to fend off the attacker. Images showed a gruesome scene onboard, with blood splashed across the cockpit and the seriously wounded pilot lying on the floor, his pained face partially covered with a mask. Machchhar told Modi he was on the ground in the cockpit when he realized the plane was going down. “And I knew in that moment – one last push, Smit! Just do it. The door is right there,” he said. “And even at that time, he was beating me up.” “And then I just opened it… and then everybody came,” he said, referring to several other passengers who then rushed into the cockpit and restrained his attacker. “I was doing this for my life, but at the same time, I knew that I couldn’t let everybody else die.” Modi praised Machchhar’s heroics, telling the veteran pilot that his “courage, patience and quick thinking… saved the lives of so many people.” “You yourself were fighting the battle of life and death,” Modi said. Machchhar is recovering at a hospital in Abu Dhabi, the capital of the United Arab Emirates (UAE). He was initially treated for his injuries in Saudi Arabia, where the diverted plane was forced to make an emergency landing. The father of two had suffered “massive blood loss” and was “severely wounded,” dentist Shota Musaev, a passenger on the flight who helped treat him, previously told CNN. His bravery “managed to prevent a 9/11 disaster,” Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu told CNN on Wednesday. Machchhar appeared emotional in the call with Modi while recalling the ordeal, and apologized to the prime minister for crying on the phone. The two later spoke in Gujarati, the language predominantly spoken by people from India’s western state of Gujarat, which is where Modi is from. Machchhar said his daughter had come to visit him in hospital but got scared seeing him in his condition. His youngest son, who is two, has not been able to meet him yet, he said. Born into a family in the textile business, becoming a pilot wasn’t Machchhar’s “childhood dream,” he told the Bona-Fide Banter podcast in 2025. Initially, he’d enrolled in a textile engineering course after school. Speaking to Modi, Machchhar said he felt a sense of pride. “Now that you have called me, I am really really proud of myself,” Machchhar said. “I wasn’t proud before this, but now I am.” His wife, Sonal Machchhar, told CNN affiliate CNN News18 that the family had not asked him yet about what happened because “we don’t want him to get flashbacks of the incident.” “We want him to fully recover, and I’m sure once he is in the right space to talk, he will share it with everyone of how the incident went on with him,” Sonal Machchhar said. What we know about the suspect The plane’s co-pilot and Machchhar’s alleged attacker has now been transferred from Saudi Arabia, where the plane landed, to the UAE, where he faces a terrorism investigation. A top UAE official on Friday described the mid-flight crisis as a “dangerous terrorist act.” Anwar Gargash, the diplomatic adviser to the UAE’s president, also cautioned against conspiracy theories as investigators look to establish the facts surrounding what happened. The suspect is an Omani national, Netanyahu told CNN Thursday. Oman and Israel do not have formal diplomatic relations, and it is not yet clear how the Omani pilot would have obtained clearance to fly to Israel. Authorities are yet to divulge the co-pilot’s identity. And there hasn’t been any confirmation of his motive or of the weapon he used in the violent altercation, though Netanyahu suggested to Fox News this might have been a knife or an axe. The Israeli prime minister said the suspect had undergone “Islamist radical indoctrination,” adding that it was too early to say whether he had connections to Iran or anyone else. He has so far stopped short of describing the incident as a terrorist act. Netanyahu said the attacker was suicidal, adding that he had called out “kill me” after being restrained by other passengers. US President Donald Trump suggested later Thursday the pilot may be linked to Iran, though he provided no details. This story had been updated with additional details.

articles.title: US lawmaker urges Starbucks to close Xinjiang outlet in China over Uyghur oppression
articles.summary: Starbucks is facing criticism in the United States after opening its first two outlets in China's Xinjiang region, with a US lawmaker urging the company
articles.body: Starbucks is facing criticism in the United States after opening its first two outlets in China's Xinjiang region, with a US lawmaker urging the company to shut them down over alleged repression of Uyghurs.John Moolenaar, chairman of the House of Representatives' Select Committee on China, said Starbucks should "immediately reverse course and close its stores" in the region.The two outlets opened this week in Xinjiang's capital, Urumqi. One is located at the city's Grand Bazaar, while the other is at the international airport.Moolenaar described Starbucks' decision to operate in Xinjiang as a "morally bankrupt decision", arguing that the company should not be doing business in a region where the US has accused Chinese authorities of widespread abuses against Uyghurs, a mainly Muslim ethnic group."This is a shocking and morally bankrupt decision by a company that prides itself on social responsibility," he said in a statement published on Thursday."There is no justifiable reason for an American company to do business in a region where the CCP (Chinese Communist Party) has detained more than a million Uyghurs and is stripping them of their faith, language, and culture."China rejects widespread accusations of abuses against Uyghurs. Beijing says its policies in Xinjiang are intended to tackle terrorism, separatism and religious extremism.Starbucks and China's Foreign Ministry had not responded to requests for comment at the time of publication. China is currently observing a week-long national holiday.Starbucks has instead presented its arrival in Xinjiang as part of its wider strategy in China. In a post on the company's official WeChat account, Starbucks said the new outlets represented more than the opening of coffee shops and were intended to offer an experience combining local culture with the needs of customers.Liu Wenjuan, Starbucks' chief executive in China, said the company would continue investing in Xinjiang.Images shared by Starbucks showed the company's branding in both English and Chinese. However, there were no obvious signs using the Uyghur language, which uses an Arabic-based script and is officially recognised alongside Chinese in Xinjiang.The controversy comes as Starbucks expands its business in China through a new ownership structure. In April 2026, the company completed a joint venture with Boyu Capital, which became the strategic investor with a 60% stake. articles.title: Watch: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay plays bus conductor, hands out tickets after expanding free travel scheme
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Friday launched the expanded 'Vettri Payanam Thittam', extending free bus travel to more categories
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Friday launched the expanded 'Vettri Payanam Thittam', extending free bus travel to more categories of services for women and transgender people across the state.Marking the launch on Gandhi Jayanti, Vijay travelled by bus in Chennai, interacted with passengers and personally handed out free tickets to women.In a light-hearted moment, college students travelling on the bus were also seen sharing Dairy Milk chocolates with the chief minister.What is Vettri Payanam scheme?The expanded scheme is expected to benefit around 84.32 lakh women every day. Beneficiaries can travel free of cost on 12,695 buses operated by seven state transport corporations, including services in the express and deluxe categories.There is no income ceiling to avail the scheme and no limit on the number of trips a beneficiary can make in a day, the state government said.The scheme, whose name is derived from the ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), meaning “victorious journey”, was earlier limited to certain categories of buses. The expanded facility now covers express, deluxe, mofussil ordinary and certain Ghat-area services.Earlier, transport minister A Vijay Tamilan Parthiban said the scheme aims to support the education, employment, livelihoods and economic empowerment of women and transgender people by ensuring that transportation costs do not become a barrier to their progress.He said the initiative was also aimed at promoting equality, adding that there should be no distinction in travel rights.Parthiban described the scheme as a “social revolution” that would help women become more independent, step out of their homes and contribute to the state’s growth."The launch is also meant to honour the principles of social justice and women's empowerment, to facilitate their participation in the economy and society, ensuring that transportation costs do not hinder their access to education, employment, or healthcare," the minister added.Get the latest India News and Live updates.
